tools.name: desktime_get_company
tools.description: The DeskTime company account this API key belongs to: company name, work schedule (start, end, duration, working days), tracking window and account timezone. GET /company.

tools.name: desktime_list_employees
tools.description: All employees of the company with their tracked time for a day, week or month: arrived/left, online, desk, at-work, productive time, productivity and efficiency, group. Starts at `date` (default today); `period` is day (default), week or month. Returned a page at a time (employee-days, sorted by dat

tools.name: desktime_get_employee
tools.description: One employee's summary for one day: name, email, group, arrived/left, late, online/offline/desk/at-work/productive time (seconds), productivity and efficiency. Without projects or apps; see desktime_get_employee_projects / _apps / _full for those. GET /employee/basic. This is employee monitoring (pe

tools.name: desktime_get_employee_projects
tools.description: One employee's day summary plus the projects and tasks they tracked time on that day. GET /employee/projects. This is employee monitoring (personal) data: ask for one day at a time and only what the user needs.

tools.name: desktime_get_employee_apps
tools.description: One employee's day summary plus the apps, websites and titles they used that day, with durations and productivity class. Lists longer than 200 entries are cut. GET /employee/apps. This is employee monitoring (personal) data: ask for one day at a time and only what the user needs.

tools.name: desktime_get_employee_full
tools.description: One employee's day summary plus both the tracked projects/tasks and the apps/websites used that day. The largest reply: prefer the narrower tools. Lists longer than 200 entries are cut. GET /employee. This is employee monitoring (personal) data: ask for one day at a time and only what the user needs

tools.name: desktime_list_projects
tools.description: Active (not archived) projects of the company with their tasks: id, name, creation time and tasks. Returned a page at a time. GET /projects.

tools.name: desktime_create_project
tools.description: WRITE: create a new project (and optionally one task in it) in the company's DeskTime account. Not idempotent: a second call with the same name makes another project. Returns the new project's id, url and tasks. POST /create-project.

tools.name: desktime_start_project
tools.description: WRITE: start tracking time on a project (and optionally a task) for the user the API key belongs to, by project name. This changes that user's tracked time and may switch away from the project currently running. Returns {started: true|false}. GET /start-project.

tools.name: desktime_stop_project
tools.description: WRITE: stop tracking time on a project (and optionally a task) for the user the API key belongs to, by project name. Returns {stopped: true|false}. GET /stop-project.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: desktime_get_employee · Private data: desktime_get_company, desktime_start_project, desktime_stop_project · Public sink: desktime_get_employee, desktime_create_project.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: desktime_get_employee · Private data: desktime_get_company, desktime_start_project, desktime_stop_project · Public sink: desktime_get_employee, desktime_create_project

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
